sources_and_currency.title: Equality Act 2010, section 40A
sources_and_currency.notes: Opened 27 October 2026. Section 40A(1): an employer must take reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of employees in the course of their employment. Inserted (26.10.2024) by the Worker Protection (Amendment of Equality Act 2010) Act 2023. The changes list shows Employment Rights Act 2025 section 20 as not yet applied to the text.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 20
sources_and_currency.notes: Opened 27 October 2026. The page was marked prospective. It inserts 'all' before 'reasonable steps' in section 40A(1). The changes box cites SI 2026/1065 regulation 3(a).

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 21
sources_and_currency.notes: Opened 27 October 2026. Prospective. Inserts Equality Act 2010 section 40(1A) to (1C). An employer permits third-party harassment only if the third party harasses the employee in the course of employment and the employer failed to take all reasonable steps. Extent England and Wales and Scotland. Commencement: SI 2026/1065 regulation 3(b).

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 22
sources_and_currency.notes: Opened 27 October 2026. Prospective. Inserts Equality Act 2010 section 40B, a power for regulations to specify steps that are to be regarded as reasonable. Commencement: SI 2026/1065 regulation 3(c). No regulations made under that power were opened.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025 (Commencement No. 6 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2026, regulation 3
sources_and_currency.notes: Regulation 3 brings sections 20, 21 and 22 into force on 30 October 2026. The same regulation commences other provisions. This checklist does not apply those other provisions.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 23
sources_and_currency.notes: Opened 27 October 2026. Inserts sexual harassment into the qualifying disclosures in section 43B of the Employment Rights Act 1996. The page says the section is in force on 6 April 2026 by SI 2026/323 regulation 3. That SI was not opened as its own page.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 25
sources_and_currency.notes: Substitutes 'six months' for 'two years' in section 108 of the Employment Rights Act 1996, and omits section 124. Not in force at Royal Assent. The page shows section 25(5) in force on 1 July 2026 for specified purposes by SI 2026/559 regulation 2. The remainder is appointed for 1 January 2027. This checklist does not apply the 1 July power.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025 (Commencement No. 4 and Transitional and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2026, regulation 3
sources_and_currency.notes: Section 25, to the extent not already in force, and Schedule 3, come into force on 1 January 2027, subject to regulation 4. This checklist does not decide an effective date of termination and does not apply regulation 4 to a person.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025, section 152
sources_and_currency.notes: Schedule 12 increases employment tribunal time limits in Great Britain from three months to six months, and in certain cases industrial tribunals in Northern Ireland. The page says the section is in force on 1 October 2026 by SI 2026/954 regulation 3, with regulation 4. This checklist does not state Northern Ireland law and does not count a time limit. The Northern Ireland limb of Schedule 12 was not applied.

sources_and_currency.title: Employment Rights Act 2025 (Commencement No. 5 and Transitional Provisions) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
sources_and_currency.notes: Regulation 3: section 152 and Schedule 12 come into force on 1 October 2026, subject to regulation 4. Regulation 4: the amendments do not apply where the relevant date is before 1 October 2026. This checklist does not identify a relevant date.

sources_and_currency.title: Plan to Make Work Pay and Employment Rights Act: timeline update
sources_and_currency.notes: Updated 22 October 2026. Confirms the harassment measures for 30 October 2026, tribunal limits on 1 October 2026, and the unfair-dismissal qualifying period and removal of the compensatory-award cap on 1 January 2027. It says breach of employment contract claims in Scotland change on 9 November 2026. That instrument was not opened. It says future dates remain subject to parliamentary processes. Non-disclosure-agreement regulations are listed for September 2027 and were not opened.

sources_and_currency.title: Acas: sexual harassment law changes
sources_and_currency.notes: Last updated 26 August 2026. From 30 October 2026 the page describes a move from 'reasonable steps' to 'all reasonable steps', and lists preparation examples. Those examples are not regulations under section 40B. The page's worked examples are not applied to a pack. Acas is not a substitute for the statute.

duties.provision: Equality Act 2010 section 40A(1). From 30 October 2026, Employment Rights Act 2025 section 20 inserts 'all'.
duties.note: In force is a date comparison. It is not a finding that this employer took, or failed to take, the steps.

duties.provision: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 21, inserting Equality Act 2010 section 40(1A) to (1C)
duties.note: The inserted subsection (1B) requires both harassment in the course of employment and a failure to take all reasonable steps. This core decides neither limb.

duties.provision: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 22, inserting Equality Act 2010 section 40B
duties.note: The power coming into force is not a list of steps. No specifying regulations were opened on 27 October 2026.

duties.provision: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 23, amending Employment Rights Act 1996 section 43B
duties.commencement_source: Commencement line on the section 23 page: SI 2026/323 regulation 3

duties.provision: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 152 and Schedule 12, by SI 2026/954 regulation 3, subject to regulation 4
duties.note: The core does not count three months or six months, and it does not identify the relevant date.

duties.provision: Employment Rights Act 2025 section 25, by SI 2026/559 regulation 3, subject to regulation 4
duties.note: Section 25 says it substitutes 'six months' for 'two years' in section 108 of the Employment Rights Act 1996. On this date that substitution is not in force. It is not applied to a person.
A timetable sentence. The regulations were not opened and are not scored.

preparation_prompts.prompt: Consider whether a standalone sexual harassment policy is useful for the organisation.
Give workers more than one way to report sexual harassment.
Provide sexual harassment training suited to the organisation.
Keep steps in place to prevent sexual harassment, rather than only responding to it.
The pack records whether third-party harassment was considered. Section 21 is a date. This row is not a finding that anyone was harassed.
The pack records whether the whistleblowing policy mentions sexual harassment. This row does not decide that a disclosure was protected.
The pack records whether probation wording was reviewed against the six-month qualifying period. This row does not apply that period to a person.

quotations.title: How to report a concern
quotations.text: Tell a manager or a fair-treatment contact. You can also use the confidential form on the staff intranet. This excerpt is synthetic.

incident_summary.signpost_for_a_person: A person may mention the Acas helpline. The agent does not contact Acas.
incident_summary.summary: Anonymised report SYN-INC-014 is for an HR lead to read. The agent has not decided what happened and has not closed it.

firm_steps_for_a_person: The HR lead reads the draft and decides whether any evidence gap is accepted.
The HR lead writes any policy change. The skeleton is headings only.
The HR lead completes the risk-assessment ratings.
A person, not the agent, replies to a worker or mentions Acas.
A disciplinary step, a suspension, or a dismissal stays in the employer's own process.
signpost: This is not legal advice. A person may mention Acas or a solicitor. The agent contacts neither.
